Information since the June meeting remains consistent with a moderate expansion and a strengthening labor market alongside subdued inflation. The June 2017 Beige Book reports economic activity expanding across Federal Reserve Districts, with consumer spending rising in multiple districts and energy activity improving on firmer oil and natural gas conditions. Labor markets are tight across districts (including Atlanta and St. Louis), with widespread reports of shortages of qualified workers for both low- and high-skilled positions; firms cite wage pressures trending up but not surging. Some districts (e.g., New York) also reported ongoing growth and steady housing activity. These Beige Book signals reinforce the FOMC’s read of solid job gains and moderate growth, while worker shortages and only modest wage pass-through help explain inflation running below 2 percent. Layering in SLOOS, which points to softer loan demand in key consumer and CRE categories and tighter consumer lending standards, suggests a mild credit headwind. Netting these, the outlook is moderately positive for activity and employment but tempered by soft inflation and slightly tighter credit conditions—consistent with maintaining a gradually accommodative stance and proceeding cautiously on balance-sheet normalization.
